clue.text: Reproducing Booth in spirit, I will be crusader against drink

indicators.note: reproducing the letters in a new form signals that they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Echoing the Salvation Army's founder William Booth, someone vows to campaign against alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to General Booth, temperance-minded founder of the Salvation Army; 'will be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner who wants alcohol banned by law is a crusader against drink.

clue.text: Whistler's just the thing to renovate

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle, and REF is his short name
IT means exactly what is wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: The painter Whistler's work is said to be ideal for sprucing a place up.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler looks like the American painter, but here it is a referee with his whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate a ship or building is to overhaul and re-equip it, which is to fit it out anew.

clue.text: Reckless uprising trapping American soldier

indicators.note: trapping means the outer word holds the other inside it
in a down clue an uprising reads the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rash means reckless

explanation.surface: A reckless rebellion catches an American serviceman in its net.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, a kind of mounted trooper.

clue.text: Rogue bishop to go without protection

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to lack something is to go without it
a guard gives protection

explanation.surface: A churchman is told to manage without any shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a scoundrel or villain, a synonym for rogue.

clue.text: Wooden actor

parts.note: a stiff performer, but also the Victorian actor-manager Sir Herbert Beerbohm ..., whose surname is made of wood

explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous actor, and a tall plant with a trunk is the source of wood.

clue.text: Bird extremely ridiculous concealing head

indicators.note: concealing its head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: most means extremely, as in 'most kind'
rich means ridiculous or outrageous, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: A bird that looks utterly absurd is hiding its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the myth that this bird buries its head in sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the large flightless African bird, the biggest living bird species.

clue.text: Gut feelings of scientist going wrong finding neutron not electron

indicators.note: going wrong signals that the letters are jumbled
'neutron not electron' tells us to put one letter in place of the other

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for an electron
N is the symbol for a neutron

explanation.surface: A physicist's hunches go awry as a neutron is detected where an electron was expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neutron not electron' turns SCIENTIST into SCINNTIST, and 'going wrong' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Instincts are intuitive urges felt rather than reasoned, the same as gut feelings.

clue.text: Cause of failure — it's the fake dosh counterfeited

indicators.note: counterfeited means forged, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruin is blamed on bogus banknotes being forged.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSH is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: An action that seems kind but dooms an enterprise is a fatal blow, a sure cause of failure.

clue.text: Murder suspect to lam scoundrel painfully

indicators.note: the hurtful thrashing suggests the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to give a villain a painful beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a suspect in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America); LAM means beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Cluedo detective board game this military character is one of six people who might be the killer.

clue.text: Be at focus? Not exactly what Sir Humphrey does

indicators.note: not exactly means not as given, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being on point is not quite the civil servant's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Humphrey Appleby is the wily mandarin in the BBC sitcom Yes Minister, famed for befuddling ministers with jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To make things unclear and confusing on purpose is the trademark trick of that evasive senior civil servant.

clue.text: Discernment shown by taking son into art gallery

indicators.note: the gallery taking in the son means he goes inside it

parts.note: the Tate is the famous art gallery in London
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Good judgement is displayed by bringing your boy to see the paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is refined judgement in matters of style and beauty, i.e. discernment.

clue.text: Dismissed footballer in wild place

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
a back is a defensive footballer

explanation.surface: A player who has been sent off stands in some untamed terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote and sparsely settled interior of Australia is a wild place.

clue.text: Cycle endlessly wearing one skimpy costume

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bike is a cycle
you are in clothes you are wearing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone rides on and on while dressed in a scanty outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit that covers very little is a skimpy costume.

clue.text: One throws weight around club after drink

indicators.note: after puts the club behind the drink

parts.note: a shot is a small measure of spirits
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A bully swings a golf club once he has had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws weight around' looks like bullying, but means literally hurling a heavy ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete in the shot put field event hurls a heavy metal ball, literally tossing a weight.

clue.text: Turner at sea portrayed dynamic content

indicators.note: content as in contents: the answer is what the words contain

explanation.surface: The painter Turner depicted energetic seascapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the marine painter J. M. W. Turner, but means something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool or swirling current in the water is something that turns at sea.

clue.text: Using numbers is a drug

parts.note: digital means working with numerical digits
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arithmetic turns out to be a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart medicine extracted from foxglove leaves is a drug.

clue.text: Clears jungle for American president with journalists

parts.note: Bush was the surname of two US presidents
hacks are journalists, especially jobbing ones

explanation.surface: Reporters accompany the US leader as land is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: To bushwhack is to cut a path through thick undergrowth, clearing jungle.

clue.text: One on the bench is bitter being kept back in lively game

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside
lively suggests the letters are jumping about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: kept back means turned to run backwards

parts.note: tart means sharp-tasting or bitter

explanation.surface: A sour juror is held back during an energetic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bench is the court's seat of justice, not a sports bench; 'lively' makes MAGE as the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judge in a lower court, someone who sits on the bench.

clue.text: Tramples partner's issue

definitions.meaning: a spouse's son from an earlier relationship is the partner's child

explanation.surface: Someone stamps on their spouse's offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it means treads down; as one word it is a husband's or wife's son.

clue.text: Disgraced cricketer's incredulous expression

definitions.meaning: Mohammad ..., a Pakistani bowler banned for spot-fixing in 2010
a scornful retort meaning 'I don't believe it'

explanation.surface: A shamed sportsman's disbelieving face.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohammad Asif was a Pakistan fast bowler jailed for spot-fixing; 'as if!' is a phrase of disbelief.

clue.text: Repeat the standard nonsense

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone echoes the usual rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Model's easy chance

definitions.meaning: someone who sits for a painter or photographer
in sport, an easy catch or shot that should not be missed

explanation.surface: An artist's model gets a simple opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter poses for a portrait; in cricket or football it is a chance so easy it must be taken.

clue.text: Without knowledge of peacekeepers a conflict heads east

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are troops of the United Nations
war is armed conflict
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers learn a war is heading east, without any warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something means having no knowledge of it.

clue.text: Friend takes a turn round motorway

indicators.note: the outer letters go round the motorway

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A pal takes a spin on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; read as letters it gives MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, often used jokily in English for a pal.

clue.text: Sportsman entertaining rabbi

definitions.meaning: a person who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at a sport
Rabbi Lionel ..., a much-loved humorous broadcaster on BBC radio

explanation.surface: An athlete plays host to a Jewish minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like a container signal, but it describes the witty rabbi.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge sports representative earns the title; Lionel Blue was a famously witty British rabbi.

clue.text: Supporter of the classics finally cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the final letter

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Support for Latin and Greek is eventually curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Atlas holds up the heavens, so he is a supporter in classical stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan of Greek mythology who bears the sky on his shoulders is a supporter from classical lore.

clue.text: Performer of ritual mostly bombastic in inclination

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: turgid means pompous or bombastic in style

explanation.surface: A ceremonial officiant is mainly pompous by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgist leads or studies church services, so someone who performs ritual.

clue.text: Breaking up rioting detains reprobate

indicators.note: a reprobate is unprincipled and wayward, so the letters go astray

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rioting holds a scoundrel in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'reprobate' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Disintegration is falling apart into fragments, i.e. breaking up.
